page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3.2xlarge is an instance within the Local SSDs family designed for I/O-intensive workloads requiring direct local storage paired with dedicated compute resources. It operates on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz using the x86_64 architecture under the KVM hypervisor. The instance is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, accompanied by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB L3 cache. It includes instruction set extensions including AVX, AVX-512, and AVX512_VNNI.

Memory and storage configuration consists of 64.0 GB of RAM, offering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Attached storage comprises a dedicated 1919 GB local SSD, providing high-capacity local disk space without relying on external volumes. Network throughput is provisioned with a 3 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the instance does not feature an integrated GPU accelerator or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark testing shows consistent mid-tier performance across general compute and memory tasks. The instance achieved an average Geekbench multi-core score of 4514.0 and a single-core score of 1185.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 8306.29. In database and caching workloads, it demonstrated 2867.75 database operations in PassMark and 6.87 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Compression workloads scored lower, with single-threaded gzip compression registering in the bottom 25 percentile. Medium-scale LLM inference for a 7B model recorded poor throughput, reflecting the constraints of non-GPU architecture for larger AI models.

From an architectural and cost-efficiency perspective, the bundled 1919 GB SSD avoids separate storage attachment overhead for high-capacity applications. The instance profile fits storage-heavy and memory-demanding workloads, including relational databases, NoSQL datastores, distributed caching layers, and search index nodes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i3.2xlarge is a storage-focused virtual instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Delivered via the KVM hypervisor, it features 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 64.0 GB of memory, and 1919 GB of integrated local SSD storage. Network performance is anchored by a 3 Gbps baseline bandwidth, with zero bundled GPUs. Synthetic and real-world benchmarks show balanced results in the mid-tier spectrum, recording 4514.0 on Geekbench multi-core, 6.87 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks, and stable memory throughput reaching 51.37 GB/s uncached reads. CPU-bound compression and larger 7B language model tasks show lower efficiency, making the hardware less optimal for intensive compute-only or heavy generative AI processing. Given the high memory capacity and direct-attached SSD volume, the instance is suited for local database engines, transactional datastores, caching clusters, and I/O-bound enterprise systems.
